ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on a billiard table, a ball is at point A and is to be shot from point A, reflected off the side cushion CD to hit ball B. Draw AC$\perp$ CD at point C, and BD$\perp$ CD at point D. Given that $\angle AEC=\angle BED$, with AC = 10cm, BD = 15cm, CD = 20cm, if the player is able to hit ball B, what is the length of DE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $AC\perp CD$ and $BD\perp CD$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACE=\angle BDE=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle AEC=\angle BED$,\\
it implies that $\triangle AEC\sim\triangle BED$,\\
Therefore, $\frac{AC}{BD}=\frac{CE}{DE}$,\\
Given that $AC=10\text{cm}$, $BD=15\text{cm}$,\\
it leads to $\frac{10}{15}=\frac{20-DE}{DE}$,\\
which results in $DE=\boxed{12}\text{cm}$,\\
Hence, the length of $DE$ is $12\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the figure is a horizontal platform edge/line segment CD, with D on the left and C on the right, and E located on the horizontal line between D and C. Point B is directly above D, and BD is a vertical line segment; point A is directly above C, and AC is a vertical line segment. In the figure, there are two oblique lines BE and AE that both intersect the base at point E, and a right angle is marked at C, indicating that AC is perpendicular to CD; the problem statement also gives that BD is perpendicular to CD. Reasoning: Because AC ⟂ CD and BD ⟂ CD, ∠ACE = ∠BDE = 90°. It is also known that ∠AEC = ∠BED, so the two right triangles △AEC and △BED are similar by AA. The corresponding sides are the vertical side AC to BD, and the base CE to DE, so AC/BD = CE/DE. It is known that AC = 10 cm, BD = 15 cm, CD = 20 cm, and E is between C and D, so CE = CD − DE = 20 − DE. Let DE = x, then 10/15 = (20 − x)/x. Solving gives 10x = 15(20 − x), that is, 25x = 300, so x = 12. Therefore DE = 12 cm.
